newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Gdansk refinery workers support a strike.
newsitem.headline: Polish Gdansk refinery workers support a strike.

text.p: A vote among workers at the Gdansk refinery, Poland's second largest, showed overwhelming support for strike action there, a union official said on Friday.
Andrzej Cenacewicz, head of the Solidarity trade union at the refinery, told Reuters that 88 percent of those polled were ready to strike to get company shares and a 17 percent pay rise.
The four unions active in the company polled 1159 employees, or 79.3 percent of all workers, over a week, he said.
"The workers of the Gdansk refinery are ready to go on strike," Cenacewicz said.

The unions demand 15 percent of the refinery's shares for free which, they say, should be given to them in line with the new privatisation law. Shares in the refinery were alloted to state-owned Nafta Polska last year.
The new privatisation law, however, does not come into force until April 8.

"The refinery's workers may be worrying unnecessarily. Once the new law is in place, it is very likely that the relevant ministry will launch procedures to give the shares to workers," a senior Nafta official, who asked not to be named, said.
Nafta has 75 percent of the refinery's shares and is itself owned by the finance ministry.

But it was not immediately clear if the remaining 25 percent, out of which the employees' stock would be paid out, were at the disposal of the finance or the treasury ministry following a recent administration reform.
The workers also want a 17 percent pay rise this year, in line with an agreement struck by employers, unions and the government in the three-sided committee last year.
The refinery's spokeswoman Ewa Sielicka said the board had no comment on the results of the referendum.
"But the board is waiting for proposals (from trade unions) on the line-up of its negotiating team," Sielicka said.
She declined to comment on what effects a potential strike could have on Gdansk's production.
